# Data & Persistence Requirements Checklist: Timesheet Management

**Purpose**: Validate the completeness, clarity, and consistency of this feature's data &
persistence requirements — the `User`/`Driver`/`Timesheet`/`TimesheetEntry` schema, Clerk-to-User
linkage, derived-vs-stored data rules, and seed-data expectations — before proceeding to
`/speckit-tasks`.
**Created**: 2026-09-04
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) · [data-model.md](../data-model.md) · [research.md](../research.md) · [contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Schema & Field Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is every persisted field on `User` traceable to a specific business need in spec.md, rather than added purely for implementation convenience? [Traceability, Data Model §User]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the cascading-delete behaviors declared on `Driver`, `Timesheet`, and `TimesheetEntry` (`onDelete: Cascade`) each traced back to a specific functional requirement (e.g., FR-014's "delete a timesheet record"), rather than left as an unexplained schema default? [Traceability, Spec §FR-014, Data Model §Relationships]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the requirement that Prisma Client access must stay strictly server-side stated with a concrete, checkable boundary (which modules may import it), rather than only as a stated intention? [Measurability, Plan §Constitution Check Principle 7]
- [ ] CHK004 Are all three unique constraints (`User.clerkUserId`, `Timesheet(userId, weekStart)`, `TimesheetEntry(timesheetId, date)`) each traced to a specific requirement or clarification, rather than introduced solely as an implementation-level "defense in depth" choice? [Traceability, Data Model §Relationships, Research §4]

## Requirement Clarity & Ambiguity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the rule that only DRIVER-role users receive a `Driver` profile stated as an explicit, reviewable requirement, rather than only implied by a schema comment? [Clarity, Data Model §Driver]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the exact boundaries of a "week" (Monday–Sunday) and how a given date is validated against them documented precisely enough that a boundary case (e.g., a date exactly on Sunday) cannot be implemented two different ways? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions, Data Model §Validation rules]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the requirement that `totalHours`, `status`, and `lastSubmittedAt` must never become stored columns stated as a firm constraint a future change could be checked against, rather than only as design rationale? [Clarity, Data Model, Research §5]
- [ ] CHK008 Are the dashboard-metrics wiring requirements specific enough about which fields become real (`activeDrivers`, `hoursThisWeek`) and which stay mocked (`inInventory`, trend percentages) to prevent an implementer from accidentally wiring the wrong one or computing an unrequested real trend? [Clarity, Research §9]

## Cross-Document Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Is the one-entry-per-date rule worded identically in intent across spec.md (FR-014a), data-model.md, and contracts/timesheet-data.md, with no drift between "replace" and "reject as duplicate"? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014a, Data Model, Contracts]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "every driver has a truck assigned" (spec.md Key Entities) consistent with `Driver.truckNumber` being a required, non-nullable field in data-model.md, with no unaddressed case (e.g., a newly onboarded driver who has not yet been assigned a truck)? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities, Data Model §Driver]

## Clerk Identity Linkage Coverage

- [ ] CHK011 Are the requirements for linking a Clerk session to a local `User` record complete enough to cover matching key, timing (when the upsert happens), and what fields get refreshed on each call? [Completeness, Contracts: user-linking.md]
- [ ] CHK012 Does the linking requirement address what happens when `currentUser()` provides no email, given `User.email` is modeled as unique-but-nullable? [Gap, Edge Case, Data Model §User]
- [ ] CHK013 Is it specified who or what is responsible for creating a `Driver` profile for a newly onboarded driver, given `getOrCreateCurrentUser()` explicitly does not create one? [Gap, Research §2]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the assumption that seeded placeholder `clerkUserId` values will never collide with a real Clerk user id stated as a validated constraint, or only as an unstated assumption? [Assumption, Research §2]

## Data Integrity & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 Does the documentation define what should happen if an Administrator-role user is ever asked to have a truck assigned (e.g., an admin who also drives)? [Gap, Edge Case, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK016 Is there a documented requirement for how the system should behave if two concurrent Server Action writes race to save the same driver/date entry? [Gap, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK017 Does the documentation specify what happens to a driver's historical `Timesheet`/`TimesheetEntry` rows if that driver's `User` record is ever removed (e.g., offboarding), or is this left undefined? [Gap, Edge Case]

## Seed Data Measurability

- [ ] CHK018 Are the seed-data requirements (roster size, status mix, truck-number uniqueness) precise enough to be verified objectively, rather than described only qualitatively (e.g., "a handful," "realistic")? [Measurability, Research §8]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the seed-data requirement specify how "current week" is determined relative to when the seed script runs, so seeded data cannot silently go stale relative to `getWeekOptions()`? [Ambiguity, Research §8]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK020 Is the assumption that this feature's three-model schema will be reused unmodified by a future Drivers-management feature (rather than requiring a breaking migration) identified as an assumption to revisit, rather than treated as settled fact? [Assumption, Research §3]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
